findings.evidence: src/app/api/auth/register/route.ts lines 25-31: if a user with the given email already exists, the handler returns NextResponse.json({ error: "Email already exists" }, { status: 409 }). The API Endpoints table documents 409 conflict behavior for other endpoints (e.g. the POST /api/plans row: 'Returns 409 if a plan for that user/year/month already exists.') but omits this for the register row.
findings.locationHint: | POST | `/api/auth/register` | Create a new user account (email, password, optional name); bcrypt-hashes the password before storage. | `src/app/api/auth/register/route.ts` |
findings.message: The register endpoint's row does not mention the 409 'Email already exists' conflict response that the route implements (route.ts lines 25-31), even though sibling rows in the same table document their conflict/not-found status codes.

findings.evidence: src/app/api/plans/route.ts POST handler (lines 26-29) calls requireUserId() and returns 401 Unauthorized if there is no session, identical to the GET handler in the same file. The doc's GET /api/plans row explicitly states 'Requires an authenticated session.' but the POST /api/plans row omits this despite enforcing the same requirement.
findings.locationHint: | POST | `/api/plans` | Create a new plan (`year`, `month`, `currency`, optional `title`). Returns 409 if a plan for that user/year/month already exists. | `src/app/api/plans/route.ts` |
findings.message: The POST /api/plans row does not state the authentication requirement that the route enforces (401 via requireUserId(), route.ts lines 26-29), even though the sibling GET /api/plans row in the same table explicitly documents this requirement.
